nodes.name: Fetch aged inventory
nodes.notes: Supabase credential sends BOTH apikey and Authorization. With apikey alone this returns 200 and an empty array - authenticated as anon, RLS hides every row, and the run looks healthy while doing nothing.

nodes.name: Check open recalls
nodes.notes: Second source: task 01's API. Allowed to fail - a VIN that will not decode must not stop the pricing review. Failures fall through as empty and are reported as 'unknown', never as 'no recalls'.

nodes.name: Retail or repair first?
nodes.notes: The two paths do different things, which is the point of branching here. A car with an open 'do not drive' recall does not get a markdown - you do not discount a car you should not be retailing, you get the recall closed first. Everything else goes to the pricing path.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ vehicle_id: $json.vehicle_id, owner_id: $json.owner_id, days_on_lot: $json.days_on_lot, holding_cost_aed: $json.holding_cost_aed, current_price_aed: $json.current_price_aed, recommended_price_aed: $json.recommended_price_aed, severity: $json.severity, rationale: $json.rationale }) }}

nodes.name: Record recommendation
nodes.notes: Idempotency. The table has UNIQUE (vehicle_id, run_date). on_conflict names that constraint as the conflict target - without it PostgREST infers the primary key and still returns 409, which is how this was found. With it, a same-day repeat returns 201 and an empty array: nothing written, nothing raised. Run the workflow twice and the second digest reports 0 new.

nodes.name: Send the digest
nodes.notes: Calls the 'Post to Discord' sub-workflow. Before this, three nodes here each carried their own copy of the webhook URL - three places to update when it rotates and three chances to miss one. Now it exists in exactly one node, in one workflow. Pick the sub-workflow in the Workflow field after import.

nodes.name: Gemini
nodes.notes: Select the Google Gemini credential here after import, and check the model name against the dropdown - it queries your account, so the list is the source of truth. maxOutputTokens is 2000 rather than a tight 200 because 2.5-series models are thinking models: reasoning tokens come out of the same budget, so a small cap can be consumed entirely before the model writes a visible word, and the call returns empty without erroring.

nodes.name: Draft the manager brief
nodes.notes: One call per run, not one per vehicle. The model writes the human framing; every number underneath is computed in code. Allowed to fail - a model outage must not stop a pricing review, so the message falls back to the deterministic summary.
